correctness.rationale: For fixed survivors r, uniform weak compositions can be generated by a Pólya urn starting with one ball at each site. Every allocation sequence with final occupancies n_i has probability product(n_i!)/[d(d+1)...(d+r-1)], so summing over the r!/product(n_i!) orders gives the exact uniform law, including the empty allocation. With t assignments already made and k occupied sites, the respective probabilities of a new site are (d-k)/d for iid uniform and (d-k)/(d+t) for the urn. Couple increments by common uniforms: a tie preserves the order by these probabilities, and an existing positive gap cannot reverse under unit increments. The deterministic first two mechanisms bound the remaining counts and conditioning on Y gives the asserted order. The one-occupied-site probabilities are d^(1-r) and d/binom(r+d-1,d-1); strictness in the nondegenerate cases follows from strict Jensen for the nonconstant Dirichlet weights, with r=0,1 and d=1 the equality cases. Conditional on the full environment, compare fresh independent branching offspring by quantiles across all generation/parent labels; nonnegative additional offspring preserve the order even for different parent counts. This uses the standard branching assumption (fresh conditional reproduction given the past, not just unconditional within-row means or marginals); allowing arbitrary dependence of the environment itself does not alter the argument. Zero is absorbing, so the finite and ultimate extinction order follows. At d=2 the formulas are for D3 and D4 and one initial colony: offspring zero has probability s and offspring two has probability A_a, giving the smallest root of (z-1)(A_a z-s)=0, with no extinction when s=0 even in the linear degeneracy. For z0 initial colonies the homogeneous probability is q_a^z0, with immediate extinction for z0=0. The binary survivor example has A3=t/2 and A4=t/3, giving exactly the stated thresholds and gap. Independent exact transition-versus-enumeration checks (python /workspace/independent_checks.py 5) passed 98 tail comparisons for 1<=d<=4 and 0<=r<=6, not a proof for all parameters.
